issues.detail: Covers mostly the happy path with few error scenarios (e.g. MCP connection failures, schema parse errors, missing WebGPU fallback, plugin load failures) and only brief edge-case notes.
Example 1 is a numbered prose outline without runnable code and Example 2 gives no concrete MCP config snippet, so the examples are somewhat simplistic.
Global npm install of @pascal-app/cli and running an authenticated MCP service that edits local project data are standard setup steps from the official package, with no malicious behavior found.

scenarios.name: script-two-room-floor-plan
scenarios.rationale: B satisfies the rubric: schema parsing, createNode(node, parentId), explicit height and thickness, [x,z] coordinates, and a door with wallId and wall-local position [4, 1.05, 0]; A computes the door position as W-4 (8) with y=0 instead of the expected [4, 1.05, 0], and also omits the 1.05 half-height y, which are the main deviations.

scenarios.name: embed-viewer-nextjs-plugin-registry
scenarios.rationale: A lists all four Pascal packages plus three, @react-three/fiber, drei and zustand, calls loadPlugin(builtinPlugin), renders <Viewer /> only after it resolves inside a full-size container, and notes WebGPU support; B gives no package names or working code and only placeholders.

scenarios.name: connect-claude-code-via-mcp
scenarios.rationale: A gives the exact `npx @pascal-app/cli editor` start command, registers an MCP entry using `pascal mcp connect`, and shows a natural-language prompt, while B gives only generic placeholders and none of the required commands.
